summary: Koshu Itabashi was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sendai Daiichi High School (~1940–1944), the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy (~1944–1945), and Tohoku University (~1950–1953), working under Teruji Ishizu from approximately 1948 to 1953.

Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Guohui Shi. He held posts at Rissho University as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2026), and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kotatsu Fujita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, working under supervisors Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura. He served at Osaka University, Hokkaido University (~1968–1991), and Sapporo Otani Junior College.
Kotetsu Yoshida is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he was attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an adviser (相談役) at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
Koun Kajiyoshi was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University.

Koun Yamada worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the First Higher School and under traditional teachers including Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, whom he succeeded (1961–1989). In 1953, he founded the Kamakura Haku-un-kai.
Koyo Sakaino worked in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held academic posts at Komazawa University and Toyo University (~1900–1933).
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He held an attested post as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at Ryukoku University in 1995.

Koyu Tamura was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned undergraduate and graduate degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University, Vạn Hạnh University, and Toyo University, where he was professor emeritus (1977–2000).

Kozen Shaku was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Senmyō. He served as abbot of Gyokuri-ji (1870–1881) and Sange-ji (1882), taught at Nagano Prefectural Northern Chugakurin (1881), and founded the Shakuson Shofukai in 1893.

Kozui Otani was a scholar of Buddhist, Iranian/Central Asian, and historical studies who studied at Kyoritsu Gakusha, Gakushuin, and under Keiun Maeda. He served as 22nd Abbot of Nishi Hongan-ji (1903–1914) and founded Kojukai in 1919.
Kripa Shankar Shukla was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Lucknow until 1959 and was attested there again in 1976.

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and University (~1853–1857) and Presidency University (~1857–1860). He later held posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist educated at Cotton University, Sanskrit College, Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jorhat College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957), and founded the Hemalata Handiqui Memorial Institute.

Krishna Mohan Banerjee worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College, Kolkata, and under Alexander Duff. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and Bishop's College (1852).

Krishna Venkateswara Sarma was an Indology and history scholar educated at University College Thiruvananthapuram and the University of Kerala under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri. He held posts at Panjab University, Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Bangalore University, and held attested posts in 1997 as Honorary Director of the Dvaita Vedanta Studies and Research Foundation and Upakulapati at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha.

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology scholar. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Krishnaswamy Nachimuthu is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. In 2021, he held an attested post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient and served as an editorial board member for Studies on the History of Śaivism.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Wartburg Theological Seminary, United Lutheran Seminary (attested 2018), and Gettysburg College (attested 2018).
